title: Forklifts in construction practice questions
description: Practice questions on forklifts in construction: rated capacity, modifications, guards, riding, elevating personnel and training (29 CFR 1926.602).

questions.question: Paragraph (c) of 29 CFR 1926.602 covers lifting and hauling equipment in construction. Which equipment does its heading leave out?

options.A: Trucks used only on paved surfaces
options.B: Equipment covered under subpart N of this part
options.C: Trucks that are rented rather than owned
options.D: Trucks used for less than one shift a day

questions.explanation: Paragraph (c) is headed "Lifting and hauling equipment (other than equipment covered under subpart N of this part)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: On a construction site, a lift truck's rated capacity is printed on a plate mounted under the seat, where the operator cannot see it from the controls. Which wording of 1926.602(c)(1)(i) does this placement fail to meet?

options.A: "firmly secured to the lifting carriage and/or forks"
options.B: "the proportion of the total load carried by any one truck"
options.C: "mounted within the periphery of the wheel"
options.D: "so as to be clearly visible to the operator"

questions.explanation: Lift trucks, stackers, etc., "shall have the rated capacity clearly posted on the vehicle so as to be clearly visible to the operator." A plate the operator cannot see does not meet that wording.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: The manufacturer provides auxiliary removable counterweights for a lift truck on a construction site. Under 1926.602(c)(1)(i), what also shall be clearly shown on the vehicle?

options.B: The date the counterweights were last weighed
options.C: The name of the person who installed the counterweights

questions.explanation: "When auxiliary removable counterweights are provided by the manufacturer, corresponding alternate rated capacities also shall be clearly shown on the vehicle. These ratings shall not be exceeded."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Modifications and loads lifted in unison
questions.question: Under 1926.602(c)(1)(ii), which modifications or additions to an industrial truck need the manufacturer's written approval?

options.A: Only those that add more than 10 percent to the truck's weight
options.B: Only those made by someone other than the manufacturer's dealer
options.C: Those which affect the capacity or safe operation of the equipment
options.D: Only those made to trucks bought after 1979

questions.explanation: "No modifications or additions which affect the capacity or safe operation of the equipment shall be made without the manufacturer's written approval." A change affecting either one is covered.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Modifications and loads lifted in unison
questions.question: A construction contractor makes an approved change to an industrial truck and updates its plates, tags and decals. What does 1926.602(c)(1)(ii) say shall in no case happen?

options.A: The original safety factor of the equipment be reduced
options.B: The truck be used by more than one operator
options.C: The truck be moved to another job site
options.D: The truck be rented to another contractor

questions.explanation: If such modifications or changes are made, the plates, tags, or decals "shall be changed accordingly. In no case shall the original safety factor of the equipment be reduced."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Modifications and loads lifted in unison
questions.question: Two industrial trucks work in unison to lift one load. What does 1926.602(c)(1)(iii) limit?

options.A: Only the lead truck's operator may control the lift
options.B: The proportion of the total load carried by any one truck shall not exceed its capacity
options.C: The trucks may travel only in reverse
options.D: No more than two trucks may share one load

questions.explanation: "If a load is lifted by two or more trucks working in unison, the proportion of the total load carried by any one truck shall not exceed its capacity."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.602(c)(1)(iv), when may a steering or spinner knob be attached to the steering wheel?

options.C: Only if the knob is removed at the end of each shift
options.D: When the steering mechanism is of a type that prevents road reactions from causing the steering handwheel to spin

questions.explanation: Steering or spinner knobs "shall not be attached to the steering wheel unless the steering mechanism is of a type that prevents road reactions from causing the steering handwheel to spin. The steering knob shall be mounted within the periphery of the wheel."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.602(c)(1)(v), which trucks shall be equipped with overhead guards?

options.A: Only trucks that carry loads above 10 feet
options.B: Only trucks used near overhead power lines
options.C: All high lift rider industrial trucks
options.D: Only trucks bought after the training deadline

questions.explanation: "All high lift rider industrial trucks shall be equipped with overhead guards which meet the configuration and structural requirements as defined in paragraph 421 of American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969, Safety Standards for Powered Industrial Trucks."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.602(c)(1)(vi), all industrial trucks in use shall meet which requirements as defined in American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969?

options.A: Only the paint and labeling requirements
options.B: Only the requirements for trucks bought new
options.D: The applicable requirements of design, construction, stability, inspection, testing, maintenance, and operation

questions.explanation: "All industrial trucks in use shall meet the applicable requirements of design, construction, stability, inspection, testing, maintenance, and operation, as defined in American National Standards Institute B56.1-1969, Safety Standards for Powered Industrial Trucks."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Riding of trucks is authorized for a task on a construction site. Under 1926.602(c)(1)(vii), what shall be provided?

options.B: A second operator to watch the rider
options.C: A written permit for each ride
options.D: A speed governor set by the rider

questions.explanation: "Unauthorized personnel shall not be permitted to ride on powered industrial trucks. A safe place to ride shall be provided where riding of trucks is authorized."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A truck is equipped with vertical only controls elevatable with the lifting carriage for lifting personnel. Which precaution is one of those 1926.602(c)(1)(viii) says shall be taken?

options.A: Personnel ride on the bare forks with a hand hold
options.B: The platform rests loosely on the forks so it can be removed quickly
options.C: Means shall be provided whereby personnel on the platform can shut off power to the truck
options.D: Personnel are lifted only while the truck travels

questions.explanation: The additional precautions include "Use of a safety platform firmly secured to the lifting carriage and/or forks" and "Means shall be provided whereby personnel on the platform can shut off power to the truck."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.602, Material handling equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does the note in 29 CFR 1926.602(d), Powered industrial truck operator training, say about the requirements for construction work?

options.A: They are left to each operator to decide
options.B: They are identical to those set forth at § 1910.178(l)
options.C: They apply only to trucks with overhead guards

questions.explanation: "Note: The requirements applicable to construction work under this paragraph are identical to those set forth at § 1910.178(l) of this chapter."
